statements.text: Tumor tissue showed broader mutational diversity than cell-free DNA, in which fewer mutations were found.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Considerable mutational diversity was observed in TT, with fewer mutations in cfDNA.
statements.note: The abstract states tissue diversity was considerable and cfDNA carried fewer mutations.

statements.text: Adapting therapy on the basis of ctDNA monitoring improved overall survival in these esophageal cancer patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: ctDNA in blood can be used for therapy monitoring of EC patients.
statements.note: Monitoring feasibility is claimed, but no survival outcome is reported.

statements.text: Longitudinal ctDNA changes were inconsistent with the patients' clinical presentation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Longitudinal ctDNA changes were consistent with clinical presentation.
statements.note: The abstract reports consistency, the opposite direction.

statements.text: Baseline cell-free DNA carried detectable mutations in 12 of the 19 patients, 63%, with a median ctDNA level of 0.4%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In baseline cfDNA, mutations were detected in 12 out of 19 patients (63%); the median ctDNA level was 0.4%.
statements.note: Both figures are reported exactly as stated.

statements.text: Mice bearing LAG-3-overexpressing melanoma cells showed prolonged survival.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Intriguingly, mice bearing LAG-3-overexpressing melanoma cells showed reduced survival but responded to anti-LAG-3 antibody therapy.
statements.note: Survival was reduced, not prolonged.

statements.text: LAG-3 overexpression drove CXCL1 and CXCL8 production in melanoma cells by enhancing TRIM28-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of IkBa, activating NF-kB.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Mechanistically, LAG-3 overexpression triggered CXCL1 and CXCL8 production of melanoma cells by enhancing TRIM28-mediated IκBα ubiquitination and degradation, which in turn activated the NF-κB pathway
statements.note: This is the mechanism the abstract reports.

statements.text: LAG-3 expression on tumor cells predicts response to anti-PD-1 monotherapy in melanoma.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study firstly identified LAG-3 as a pro-tumor factor and a predictor for anti-LAG-3 immunotherapy efficacy.
statements.note: The prediction claim concerns anti-LAG-3 therapy; anti-PD-1 is never tested.

statements.text: Depleting myeloid-derived suppressor cells cancelled the pro-tumor effect of tumor cell-derived LAG-3.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Notably, depletion of MDSCs counteracted the pro-tumor activity of tumor cell-derived LAG-3.
statements.note: MDSC depletion counteracted the effect, as stated.

statements.text: Combining cfDNA with matched white blood cell DNA avoided germline or hematopoietic false-positive calls in 40% of patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The combined cfDNA and WBC analysis prevented false-positives due to germline or hematopoietic variants in 40% of patients.
statements.note: The 40% figure is reported for exactly this comparison.

statements.text: Standard-of-care radiological response evaluation predicted overall survival better than longitudinal ctDNA analysis.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Longitudinal analyses of ctDNA were more predictive of overall survival than standard-of-care radiological response evaluation.
statements.note: The abstract ranks ctDNA above radiology, the reverse of this claim.

statements.text: Switching treatment on the basis of the detected ctDNA resistance mutations lengthened progression-free survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: ctDNA mutations related to primary or acquired resistance to panitumumab were identified in 42% of patients.
statements.note: Resistance mutations were detected; no ctDNA-guided treatment change or its outcome is reported.

statements.text: Sequencing the patient-matched tumor tissue added no information beyond the cfDNA and white blood cell analysis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patient-matched tumor tissue sequencing did not provide additional information.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: Patients in the CICLADES cohort with high tumor mutation burden had shorter overall survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Tumor Mutation Burden (TMB) and hypermutation were estimated and compared between samples.
statements.note: TMB was compared across cohorts only; no survival analysis is reported.

statements.text: Tumor mutation burden was comparable between the CICLADES and CBSM groups, while the MSKCC population carried a significantly higher burden than both.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: TMB was similar between the CICLADES and CBSM groups, however the MSKCC population showed a significantly higher TMB than both.
statements.note: This is the reported TMB comparison.

statements.text: Nine signatures were extracted in total, among them the recurring substitution signatures SBS1, SBS2 and SBS5.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Nine signatures were extracted, with recurring Single Base Substitutions (SBS) signatures like SBS1, SBS2 and SBS5.
statements.note: The count and the named signatures match the abstract.

statements.text: APOBEC-enriched samples carried a significantly lower mean number of mutations than non-enriched samples in each cohort.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The mean number of mutations was significantly higher in enriched samples for each analyzed cohort.
statements.note: The mean was higher, not lower, in enriched samples.

statements.text: Knocking down aub specifically at the larval neuromuscular junction raised transposable element expression, Copia among them.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Tissue-specific knockdown of aub at the LNMJ resulted in increased TE expression, including Copia
statements.note: Stated as a result of the tissue-specific knockdown.

statements.text: Genetic reporters and antibody staining showed AUB to be absent from the larval neuromuscular junction.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Data from genetic reporters and antibody staining show that AUB is expressed and localized to the LNMJ.
statements.note: AUB was expressed and localized there, not absent.

statements.text: Restoring Copia repression in aub knockdown larvae rescued their synapse number.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These phenotypes are consistent with the upregulation of Copia , a negative regulator of synapse growth.
statements.note: Consistency with Copia upregulation is argued, but no rescue experiment is reported.

statements.text: Reducing aub lowered synapse number and impaired motor function and lifespan, opposite to the overgrowth seen on Copia depletion.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In contrast to the synaptic overgrowth seen with Copia depletion [1], aub reduction caused a decrease in synapse number and impaired motor function and lifespan.
statements.note: Both the phenotype and the contrast are reported.

statements.text: Copy number analysis gave ichorCNA tumor fractions spanning 0% to 12.8% in the plasma samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with ichorCNA-derived tumor fractions ranging from 0% to 12.8%
statements.note: That is the reported range of ichorCNA tumor fractions.

statements.text: FLARE detected ctDNA at lower tumor fractions than a short-read fragmentomics pipeline run on the same samples.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: However, most current methods are designed for short-read sequencing, limiting their applicability to third-generation technologies.
statements.note: Short-read methods appear only as motivation; no head-to-head comparison was run.

statements.text: End-motif analysis of 5' 4-mer frequencies combined with non-negative matrix factorization showed A-end and G-end patterns predominating.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: End-motif analysis based on 5'4-mer frequencies, combined with non-negative matrix factorization (NMF), identified predominant A-end and G-end patterns
statements.note: These are the predominant end motifs reported.

statements.text: Tumor fraction estimates from methylation-based fragmentomic features showed no correlation with clinical response.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Tumor fraction estimates derived from methylation-based fragmentomic features showed concordant trends, providing an independent measure of tumor burden and correlating with clinical response.
statements.note: They did correlate with clinical response.

statements.text: The two dominant ICE groups rarely occur together in the same Porphyromonas gingivalis genome.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We found that these elements comprise at least five distinct groups, two of which dominate and frequently co-occur in Pg genomes, inserting into distinct characteristic insertion sites.
statements.note: The two dominant groups frequently co-occur.

statements.text: No exact matches were found between ICE sequences and Pg CRISPR spacers, unlike the extensive targeting seen for Pg phages.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In contrast to the extensive CRISPR-Cas defense targeting we observed for Pg phages, we detected no exact matches between ICE sequences and Pg CRISPR spacers.
statements.note: Stated directly as a result.

statements.text: More than 90% of the Pg genomes examined carried at least one integrative and conjugative element.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We discovered that ICEs are pervasive in Pg genomes, with >90% of genomes harboring at least one ICE.
statements.note: The >90% figure is reported.

statements.text: Pg strains carrying ICEs caused more severe periodontal disease than ICE-free strains.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Using marker-gene analysis of enrichment-culture mini-metagenomes from subjects with periodontal disease we detected representatives of these dominant Pg ICE groups, as well as others, in recent clinical samples.
statements.note: ICEs were detected in clinical samples; no severity comparison between strains is made.

statements.text: dd-cfDNA alone discriminated rejection with an AUC of 0.79 in the derivation cohort and 0.80 in the validation cohort.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.79 (95% confidence interval, 0.73 to 0.84) and 0.80 (95% confidence interval, 0.72 to 0.87) in the derivation and validation cohorts, respectively
statements.note: Those are the reported AUCs for dd-cfDNA alone.

statements.text: Of the 482 biopsies that post-test probabilities would have safely avoided, 437, or 91%, were protocol biopsies.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 482 biopsies would have been safely avoided using post-test probabilities, with 437 (91%) of these being protocol biopsies
statements.note: Both counts appear in the results.

statements.text: Managing patients by dd-cfDNA-based post-test risk preserved graft function as well as biopsy-guided care did.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our study confirmed the strong association between dd-cfDNA% and rejection after kidney transplantation.
statements.note: Risk reclassification was modelled; no graft-function outcome of such management is reported.

statements.text: Adding clinical parameters to dd-cfDNA lowered the area under the curve in both cohorts.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Combining dd-cfDNA with clinical parameters improved the above area under the receiver operating characteristic curves to 0.82 and 0.87, respectively.
statements.note: The combination improved the AUCs.

statements.text: The isolates came from a healthy 32-year-old man who had two infection episodes six months apart, first the left ear and then the left eye.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we characterized CoNS isolates obtained over time from a healthy 32-year-old male who experienced two infection episodes 6 months apart (left ear, followed by the left eye)
statements.note: The participant and the two episodes are described exactly so.

statements.text: The mosaic SCCmec type IV element was identified in a Staphylococcus epidermidis isolate from the infected eye.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A non-typable, mosaic SCCmec type IV element homologous to SCCmec IVa/IVn was identified in the multidrug-resistant S. capitis subsp. urealyticus ST1 isolate E_e2, recovered from the infected ear.
statements.note: The element was in an S. capitis ear isolate, not an eye S. epidermidis one.

statements.text: The three Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates from the symptomatic left eye shared a novel sequence type, ST1284.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: while the three S. epidermidis isolates shared a novel sequence type, ST1284
statements.note: Reported as a novel sequence type shared by the three eye isolates.

statements.text: Sequencing revealed plasmids carrying additional resistance genes in the six isolates.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Six CoNS isolates were recovered, tested for antimicrobial susceptibility and subjected to whole-genome sequencing.
statements.note: Sequencing and susceptibility testing are reported; plasmid content is never described.

statements.text: The breed-specific ERV insertion polymorphisms were associated with differences in milk yield between cattle breeds.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: PCR genotyping revealed breed-specific polymorphisms in both cattle and buffalo, suggesting ongoing retroviral influence
statements.note: Polymorphisms were genotyped across breeds; no production trait was examined.

statements.text: Of the 22 ERV groups identified, 20 were beta-retroviruses of Class II and two were gamma-retroviruses of Class I.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A total of 22 distinct ERV groups were identified, consisting of 20 beta-retroviruses (Class II) and two gamma-retroviruses (Class I).
statements.note: The counts and classes match the abstract.

statements.text: The ERVs were enriched in transcribed regions and depleted at regulatory loci.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: While ERVs were depleted in transcribed regions likely due to purifying selection, they were enriched at regulatory loci, indicating their role in shaping host gene networks.
statements.note: The two distributions are the reverse of this.

statements.text: Buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) harboured 838 ERVs against 575 in cattle (Bos taurus).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with Bubalus bubalis (buffalo) housing 838 ERVs compared to 575 in Bos taurus (cattle)
statements.note: These are the reported ERV counts for the two species.

statements.text: Tight junction integrity was disrupted for 7 days and as far as 100 micrometres from the ablation zone.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: LITT transiently disrupted TJ integrity for 7 days up to 100 µm away from the ablation zone.
statements.note: The duration and distance are reported exactly.

statements.text: LITT lowered circulating tumor DNA levels in mouse plasma over the two weeks after the procedure.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: LITT facilitated ctDNA detection in mouse plasma at 1 h, 3 days, 7 days, and 14 days post-procedure.
statements.note: LITT facilitated rather than reduced ctDNA detection.

statements.text: Mice treated with LITT survived longer than untreated tumor-bearing mice.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Using our previously developed LITT mouse model, we employed single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) to investigate gene expression changes in endothelial cells following LITT in the naive mouse brain.
statements.note: The experiments characterised barrier changes in naive brain; no survival comparison is reported.

statements.text: Caveolae-mediated transcytosis in endothelial cells stayed elevated for 21 days, peaking at 14 days, partly through suppression of Mfsd2a.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Further, LITT increased caveolae-mediated transcytosis in endothelial cells for 21 days, peaking at 14 days, in part due to suppression of the transcytosis inhibitor Mfsd2a.
statements.note: Duration, peak and mechanism are as stated.

statements.text: The framework requires matched normal samples to infer mutation copy number and multiplicity from targeted panels.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: infers mutation copy number and multiplicity directly from clinical targeted sequencing panels without requiring matched normal samples
statements.note: The method works without matched normals.

statements.text: Twenty-six biomarkers were recurrently associated with metastatic spread in 10 tumour types, and 20 predicted organ-specific tropism in five.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Additionally, 26 biomarkers were recurrently associated with metastatic spread in 10 tumour types, and 20 predicted organ-specific metastatic tropism in 5 tumour types.
statements.note: Both counts are reported as stated.

statements.text: Mutant dosage biomarkers predicted which patients responded to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: gene mutant dosage patterns as independent predictors of prognosis, metastatic potential, and site-specific dissemination across diverse solid tumours
statements.note: Prognosis and metastasis were analysed; treatment response was not.

statements.text: Stratifying more than 20,000 patients by mutant dosage yielded 46 tumour type-specific biomarkers predictive of overall survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we identified 46 tumour type–specific biomarkers predictive of overall survival
statements.note: That is the reported number of survival biomarkers.

statements.text: The method was applied to 60 melanoma and 21 acute myeloid leukaemia patient samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Applied to 60 melanoma and 21 acute myeloid leukaemia patient samples, the method identifies heterogeneous clonal responses
statements.note: Those are the sample numbers given.

statements.text: Patients whose tumours contained resistant clones were moved to alternative therapies in a prospective trial.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These results demonstrate that modelling tumour evolution and clonal diversity is crucial for accurate drug-response prediction and provides a foundation for more effective, clone-aware precision oncology.
statements.note: The work is computational; no prospective treatment allocation is described.

statements.text: scClone2DR predicts drug response only for whole tumours, not for individual clones.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we introduce scClone2DR, a probabilistic multi-modal framework that predicts drug responses at the level of individual tumour clones
statements.note: Prediction is explicitly at the level of individual clones.

statements.text: In simulations the method recovered true drug effects and clonal sensitivities substantially better than competing approaches.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In simulations, scClone2DR substantially outperforms alternatives in recovering true drug-effects and clonal sensitivities.
statements.note: Stated as the simulation result.

statements.text: Seminoma patients with KIT mutations responded better to imatinib than those without them.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study provided a comprehensive molecular and genetic profiling of seminoma including key genetic alterations, affected pathways, and potential therapeutic strategies.
statements.note: Therapeutic options are discussed in principle; no treatment response data are reported.

statements.text: The alterations pointed to the KIT/RAS/MAPK pathway but gave no indication of PI3K/AKT/mTOR involvement.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: These suggest involvement within the KIT/RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR (PAM) pathways for seminoma development.
statements.note: Both pathways are implicated, not only KIT/RAS/MAPK.

statements.text: KIT was the most frequently mutated gene at 22.6%, ahead of KRAS at 17.1% and MTOR at 5.1%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The most mutated genes included KIT (22.6%), KRAS (17.1%), and MTOR (5.1%)
statements.note: These are the reported mutation frequencies.

statements.text: BRD4 mutations appeared only in metastatic samples, while KMT2C, STAG2, ALK, AXL and EGFR appeared only in primary samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: BRD4 mutations were found only in metastatic samples while KMT2C , STAG2 , ALK , AXL , and EGFR were only found in primary samples
statements.note: The split between metastatic and primary samples is as stated.

statements.text: Hemolysis testing showed the saline-replaced fermentation supernatant had high hemolytic activity.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Hemolysis tests proved that the physiological saline-replaced fermentation supernatant possessed low hemolytic activity.
statements.note: Hemolytic activity was low.

statements.text: Scanning electron microscopy showed thanatin damaging bacterial cell membranes and causing lysis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Scanning electron microscopy further revealed that thanatin caused damage to bacterial cell membranes and led to cell lysis.
statements.note: Stated as the microscopy result.

statements.text: Thanatin yield from the engineered yeast exceeded that of established Escherichia coli expression systems.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we constructed a heterologous expression system for thanatin in Saccharomyces cerevisiae CENPK2 using both PiggyBac (PB) and Ty2 retrotransposon systems
statements.note: Yeast expression is demonstrated; no yield comparison with another host is given.

statements.text: Strains carrying both the PiggyBac and Ty2 systems inhibited bacteria more strongly than strains carrying only one.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Notably, strains harboring both PB and Ty2 systems exhibited stronger antibacterial activity than those with a single system.
statements.note: The dual-system comparison is reported this way.

statements.text: Embryos selected using spent-medium cfDNA results achieved higher implantation rates than embryos selected on morphology.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Overall, SCM-based cfDNA analysis exhibited promise as a complementary tool for embryo selection in IVF workflows.
statements.note: A role in embryo selection is proposed; no implantation or pregnancy outcome is reported.

statements.text: RHD exon 7 amplified in 6 of 15 samples and exon 10 in 11 of them, with only partial agreement between exons.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: RHD gene amplification was detected in 6 of 15 samples for exon 7 and in 11 samples for exon 10, with partial concordance between exons.
statements.note: Both counts and the partial concordance are stated.

statements.text: SRY amplified in 16 of 31 spent culture medium samples and largely matched the clinical sex data.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: SRY amplification was observed in 16 of 31 samples and was largely consistent with clinical sex data.
statements.note: The count and the agreement with clinical data are reported.

statements.text: The correlation between maternal age and MT-CYB levels was statistically significant.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A moderate positive correlation trend was noted between maternal age and MT-CYB levels (r=0.46; P=0.354).
statements.note: With P = 0.354 the abstract describes only a trend, not significance.

statements.text: The convolutional autoencoder reached 84.6% cross-validated accuracy with an AUC of 0.87.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: achieving 84.6% cross-validated accuracy (AUC = 0.87)
statements.note: Those are the reported classification metrics.

statements.text: Selected latent features showed no correlation with serum neurofilament light chain.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Selected latent features were reproducible across an independent same-subject experimental batch and correlated with serum neurofilament light chain
statements.note: The features did correlate with neurofilament light chain.

statements.text: Mass spectrometry found the protein corona of ALS samples enriched in adaptive-immune and inflammatory proteins.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: revealing an ALS-biased protein corona enriched in adaptive-immune and inflammatory proteins
statements.note: Stated as the mass spectrometry finding.

statements.text: The spectral signature separated ALS patients from people with other neurodegenerative diseases.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: was tested on serum from 20 ALS patients and 19 sex-matched controls (n = 39, TargetALS)
statements.note: The comparison was ALS versus sex-matched controls; no other disease group was tested.

statements.text: In the tumor-informed setting, adding genome-wide features substantially improved detection in every cancer type examined.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: addition of GW features was marginally beneficial except in lung cancer
statements.note: The benefit was marginal, and lung cancer was an exception.

statements.text: Assay performance was maximised with single-stranded DNA ligation, cfDNA input of at least 15 ng, post-UMI depth of 2500X or more, and many tracked mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Optimal parameters to maximize assay performance included single-stranded DNA ligation technology, cfDNA input ≥ 15 ng, post-UMI sequencing depth ≥ 2500X, and high number of tracked mutations.
statements.note: These are the optimal parameters listed.

statements.text: The hybrid capture workflow costs less per sample than the amplicon-based assay.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The new methodology offers a streamlined and scalable solution for both comprehensive liquid biopsy profiling and longitudinal MRD tracking in routine clinical practice.
statements.note: Scalability is claimed; no cost comparison is given.

statements.text: From surveillance samples, HYB predicted recurrence with 100% sensitivity in colorectal cancer and 96.0% in hepatocellular carcinoma, against 90.0% and 80.0% for AMP.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Surveillance ctDNA determined by the HYB workflow had superior sensitivity to predict recurrence in both CRC (AMP: 90.0%, HYB: 100%) and HCC (AMP: 80.0%, HYB: 96.0%).
statements.note: All four sensitivities are reported as stated.

statements.text: Benthic sediment metagenomes from 59 monitoring stations across 1,150 km yielded predicted ARGs covering 26 antibiotic classes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We analyzed the metagenomes of benthic sediments from 59 monitoring stations across a 1,150 km distance of the Baltic Sea
statements.note: Station count, distance and the 26 antibiotic classes are all reported.

statements.text: Sediment ARG abundance tracked the volume of antibiotics used in the countries bordering each sampled region.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The combined effects of salinity and temperature gradients, alongside nutrient availability, created a complex environmental landscape that shaped the diversity and distribution of the predicted ARGs.
statements.note: Salinity, temperature and nutrients were tested; antibiotic use data were not analysed.

statements.text: Resistome diversity was highest in the southern Baltic and in the dead zones, declining towards the north.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We observed spatial variation in its resistance profile, with higher resistome diversity in the northern regions and a decline in the dead zones and the southern areas.
statements.note: Diversity was higher in the north and declined in the south and dead zones.

statements.text: Salinity had the strongest influence on microbial communities and predicted ARG composition.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Salinity predominantly influenced microbial communities and predicted ARG composition
statements.note: Salinity is named as the predominant influence.

statements.text: Both paired worms and male worms alone significantly altered the miRNA expression profile of hepatic stellate cells.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Both paired worms and male worms significantly altered the miRNA expression profile of hepatic stellate cells.
statements.note: Stated directly for both worm conditions.

statements.text: Pathway enrichment placed the predicted targets of hsa-miR-103a-3p mainly in Wnt and Notch signalling pathways.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the potential target genes of hsa-miR-103a-3p were mainly enriched in AMP-activated protein kinase, mechanistic target of rapamycin, tumor necrosis factor, insulin signaling, and cellular senescence pathways
statements.note: The enriched pathways listed are different ones.

statements.text: Blocking hsa-miR-103a-3p in hepatic stellate cells reduced their activation into fibrogenic myofibroblasts.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: hsa-miR-103a-3p may be associated with fibrogenic responses and may have potential relevance to hepatocellular carcinoma-related processes
statements.note: An association with fibrogenic responses is proposed; no inhibition experiment is reported.

statements.text: In TCGA data hsa-miR-103a-3p had diagnostic value in hepatocellular carcinoma and was associated with alpha-fetoprotein level and Ishak fibrosis score.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: hsa-miR-103a-3p had diagnostic value in hepatocellular carcinoma and was associated with alpha-fetoprotein level, albumin level, Ishak fibrosis score, pathological stage, histological type, and tumor status
statements.note: Both associations appear in the reported list.

statements.text: Sixteen of the 83 patients, 19.3%, were ctDNA positive with mutations in one or more genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Sixteen (19.3 %) patients were considered ctDNA positive with mutations in one or more genes.
statements.note: The count and percentage are as reported.

statements.text: ctDNA positivity was more common in patients whose tumours were of the p53-abnormal molecular subtype.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Tumor tissue from 56 of the 83 patients was subjected to whole-exome sequencing, and clinical data were collected for oncological outcome assessment.
statements.note: Tumour sequencing served concordance and outcome analysis; molecular subtypes are not reported.

statements.text: Recurrence was significantly more frequent in patients with preoperative ctDNA, 37.5% versus 11.9%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The preoperative presence of ctDNA was associated with a significantly higher rate of recurrence (37.5 % vs 11.9 %, P = 0.024).
statements.note: Both recurrence rates are reported with P = 0.024.

statements.text: Once known histopathologic risk factors were controlled for, ctDNA positivity was no longer an independent predictor of recurrence.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: positive ctDNA status remained an independent predictor of recurrence also when controlling for other known histopathologic risk factors (HR 5.49, 95 % CI 1.5-20, P = 0.010)
statements.note: It remained an independent predictor after adjustment.

statements.text: Plasmids were the dominant mobile genetic element class identified by the pipeline.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The pipeline identified transposons as the dominant MGE class
statements.note: Transposons, not plasmids, were dominant.

statements.text: Transposon-associated ARGs differed most consistently between environments, with ANOVA p = 0.0017 and Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.018.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Transposon-associated ARGs showed the most consistent environmental differentiation (ANOVA p = 0.0017; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.018)
statements.note: Both p values are reported for transposon-associated ARGs.

statements.text: The Random Forest model reached an AUC of 0.82, and SHAP analysis identified transposon abundance as the main driver of ARG dissemination.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The Random Forest (RF) model achieved an AUC of 0.82, and subsequent feature importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses revealed that transposon abundance is the primary factor driving ARG dissemination
statements.note: Both the AUC and the leading feature are stated.

statements.text: MobiRes ranked wastewater as the environment with the highest overall resistome risk.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The pipeline was evaluated using a wide range of publicly available metagenomic datasets spanning diverse environments, including wastewater, poultry, soil, sediments, and human fecal samples.
statements.note: Those environments were analysed, but no ranking of overall risk is given.

statements.text: Strain KP_WXD was resistant to every beta-lactam agent tested.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: K. pneumoniae KP_WXD strain was resistant to all tested β-lactam agents.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: KP_WXD formed weaker biofilms than the reference strains ST11-KL64 and NTUH-k2044.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: while its biofilm formation ability was stronger than that of both strains
statements.note: Its biofilm formation was stronger than both references.

statements.text: Sequence type ST105 is spreading in hospitals in the region where KP_WXD was isolated.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Uncommon multilocus sequence types (MLSTs) of NDM-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae may pose a significant threat to patients, although they are often overlooked in surveillance studies.
statements.note: A single isolate was characterised; no prevalence or surveillance data are reported.

statements.text: Both the NDM-1 and CTX-M carrying plasmids transferred to E. coli J53 by conjugation without significant fitness cost to the recipient.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: both bla NDM-1 and bla CTX-M -harboring plasmids were transferable to E. coli J53 by conjugation without significant fitness cost on the recipient strain
statements.note: Transfer and the absence of fitness cost are both reported.

statements.text: Knocking down WWP1 in SKOV3 cells restored their sensitivity to cisplatin.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Multicolor immunofluorescence assay was used to analyze the immune markers in SKOV3 and SKOV3/DDP cell xenografts in nude mice.
statements.note: The resistant line served immune marker staining; no knockdown or drug sensitivity test is reported.

statements.text: RNA-seq of WWP1-overexpressing SKOV3 cells and immunofluorescence in tumor-bearing mice agreed with the bioinformatics findings.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: RNA-seq analysis of WWP1-overexpressing SKOV3 cells and immunofluorescence assay of the tumor-bearing mice yielded findings consistent with those of bioinformatics analysis.
statements.note: The experimental work is reported as consistent with the bioinformatics.

statements.text: High WWP1 expression was associated with a favourable prognosis, unlike Stage IV disease.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: High WWP1 expression levels and Stage IV disease were both associated with a poor prognosis
statements.note: High WWP1 expression carried a poor prognosis, like Stage IV disease.

statements.text: Patients with high WWP1 expression had a significantly lower overall survival rate, at P = 0.0012.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The patients with high WWP1 expression levels had significantly lower overall survival rate ( P =0.0012).
statements.note: The survival difference and its P value are reported.

statements.text: Hundreds of anti-CRISPR homologs were tested for inhibition of Cas9 from Streptococcus pyogenes and Staphylococcus aureus.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we characterized hundreds of Acr homologs for their ability to inhibit Cas9 proteins from Streptococcus pyogenes and Staphylococcus aureus
statements.note: That is the scale and the two Cas9 orthologs tested.

statements.text: Three previously unknown Acr families were uncovered, found through fusion to helix-tail-helix domains or presence in operons with other Acrs.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our work also uncovered three novel Acr families through their fusion to helix-tail-helix domains or their presence in operons with other Acrs.
statements.note: The count and the two routes of discovery are stated.

statements.text: The newly described Acr proteins inhibited Cas12a as well as Cas9.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings reveal the patterns of functional diversity in Acr families and greatly expand the arsenal of Acr genes available for biotechnological applications.
statements.note: Only Cas9 orthologs were assayed; other Cas nucleases are not mentioned.

statements.text: Every Acr family examined showed inhibition patterns consistent with specialization to different Cas9 orthologs.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: several anti-CRISPR families displayed deep conversation of the ability to inhibit a given Cas9, indicating that their evolutionary trajectory has not involved specialization across the family to different Cas9 orthologs
statements.note: Several families showed conservation rather than specialization.

statements.text: SiMSen-Seq and the AVENIO panel agreed on PIK3CA mutation status in 92.6% of cases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: High concordance (92.6%) was observed between SSS and AVENIO for PIK3CA mutations.
statements.note: That is the reported concordance between the two assays.

statements.text: Beyond PIK3CA hotspots, the AVENIO panel found no additional actionable alterations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: AVENIO identified additional actionable alterations, including ESR1 (17.5%) and PI3K pathway alterations (40.6%)
statements.note: The panel did identify additional actionable alterations.

statements.text: Patients with plasma ESR1 alterations had shorter progression-free survival on their next line of therapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings support broader ctDNA profiling in clinical practice while highlighting accessibility challenges.
statements.note: The study compared assays; no outcome data by alteration status are reported.

statements.text: The study analysed 161 plasma samples from 146 patients, taken before they started a new line of palliative therapy.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: analyzing 161 plasma samples from 146 patients before initiating a new line of palliative therapy
statements.note: Sample and patient numbers and the timing are as stated.

statements.text: Most of the 12 MRD-negative patients went on to relapse.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Only 1/12 MRD-negative patients relapsed.
statements.note: Just one of the twelve relapsed.

statements.text: Every patient with an early molecular response reached end-of-treatment complete metabolic response, against 12.5% of those without one.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: was predictive of end-of-treatment complete metabolic response (CMR; EMR rate 100% vs. no EMR 12.5%, p = 0.0014)
statements.note: The 100% versus 12.5% comparison is reported with p = 0.0014.

statements.text: Baseline ctDNA level correlated with the patients' International Prognostic Index score.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Next generation sequencing (NGS) of cell free tumour DNA (ctDNA) provides a snapshot of lymphoma mutations correlating with tumour burden.
statements.note: ctDNA is tied to tumour burden, but no clinical risk score comparison is reported.

statements.text: Baseline somatic mutations were detected in all 17 patients, and 13 carried phased variants usable for greater assay sensitivity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Somatic mutations were detected at baseline in 17/17 patients, including 13 with phased variants that could be leveraged for enhanced assay sensitivity.
statements.note: Both counts are as reported.

statements.text: CEACAM6 expression was significantly negatively associated with CD4+ Th1 cell abundance across pan-gastrointestinal cancers.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The CEACAM6 expression was significantly negatively associated with the abundance of CD4 + Th1 cells across pan-gastrointestinal cancers.
statements.note: The direction and significance are as stated.

statements.text: Knocking down CEACAM6 in gastric cancer cell lines reduced their invasion in vitro.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: CEACAM6 could promote angiogenesis/metastasis and suppress anti-tumor immunity.
statements.note: The inference rests on multi-omics association analyses; no knockdown experiment is reported.

statements.text: In TCGA data CEACAM6 was underexpressed in pan-gastrointestinal cancers.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Based on TCGA data, CEACAM6 was found to be overexpressed in pan-gastrointestinal cancers.
statements.note: It was overexpressed.

statements.text: Spatial transcriptomics tied CEACAM6 expression positively to malignant cells and negatively to plasma cells.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: spatial transcriptomics data revealed that CEACAM6 expression was significant positively associated with malignant cells, while there was a negative correlation was observed with between CEACAM6 expression and plasma cells
statements.note: Both spatial associations are reported.

statements.text: The mutation detection rate was significantly lower in CTC samples than in tissue and ctDNA samples.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The mutation detection rate in CTCs samples was significantly higher than that in tissue and ctDNA samples.
statements.note: Detection in CTCs was higher, not lower.

statements.text: CTC counts separated gastric cancer patients from others with 97.29% sensitivity and 97.73% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of 97.29% and 97.73%, respectively
statements.note: Those are the reported diagnostic metrics.

statements.text: Mutations in CTCs matched tissue mutations in 24.32% of cases and ctDNA mutations in 19.05%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The concordance rate between CTCs and tissue mutations was 24.32%, while the concordance rate between CTCs and ctDNA mutations was 19.05%.
statements.note: Both concordance rates are as reported.

statements.text: CTC counts fell after gastrectomy in the 68 gastric cancer patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Sixty-eight GC patients underwent CTCs detection.
statements.note: CTCs were counted and related to tumour features; no post-surgical follow-up is reported.

statements.text: Yeast strains lacking DRT2 grow more slowly because of unrestrained Ty1 prime insertions.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Ty1' retromobility analyses demonstrate DRT2 restriction factor functionality, and northern blot and RNA-seq analysis indicate that DRT2 is transcribed in multiple strains.
statements.note: Restriction of retromobility is shown; no growth or fitness consequence is measured.

statements.text: Velocity cosedimentation showed Drt2 associating with Ty1 prime virus-like particles or assembly complexes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Velocity cosedimentation profiles indicate an association between Drt2 and Ty1' virus-like particles or assembly complexes.
statements.note: Stated as the cosedimentation result.

statements.text: Ty1 prime retromobility fell as copy number rose, just as it does for Ty1 canonical.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Unlike Ty1 canonical, Ty1' retromobility increases with copy number
statements.note: Retromobility increases with copy number, and this differs from Ty1 canonical.

statements.text: DRT2 arose by domestication of a Ty1 prime GAG gene and retains the C-terminal domain of capsid.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: DRT2 arose through domestication of a Ty1' GAG gene and contains the C-terminal domain of capsid
statements.note: Both the origin and the retained domain are stated.

statements.text: 45S rDNA arrays accumulated oxidized cytosines strongly and consistently, 5fC and 5caC above all, in transcriptionally active nucleolar organizing regions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In contrast, 45S rDNA arrays display strong and consistent accumulation of oxi-mCs, especially 5fC and 5caC, in transcriptionally active nucleolar organizing regions
statements.note: This is the reported rDNA pattern.

statements.text: Oxidized cytosines were restricted to LTR retrotransposons among the repeat classes examined.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we identify widespread association of oxi-mCs across major repeat classes, including LTR retrotransposons, DNA transposons, satellite repeats, and ribosomal DNA (rDNA)
statements.note: The association spanned several repeat classes, not only LTR retrotransposons.

statements.text: Transposable elements carried oxidized cytosines roughly in line with their genomic abundance, while satellite DNA was selectively overrepresented.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: While transposable elements largely reflect genomic abundance, satellite DNA shows selective and context-dependent overrepresentation, particularly within the major centromeric repeat clusters (STAR-C)
statements.note: The contrast between TEs and satellite DNA is as stated.

statements.text: The sex chromosomes of Silene latifolia carried more oxidized cytosines than the autosomes.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: a dioecious plant with heteromorphic sex chromosomes
statements.note: The sex chromosomes appear only as background; no comparison with autosomes is reported.

statements.text: The analysis covered 1,054 publications, with research activity rising sharply from 2015 onward.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The analysis encompassed a total of 1,054 publications, demonstrating a marked escalation in research activity since 2015.
statements.note: The publication count and the 2015 inflection are reported.

statements.text: Keyword analysis resolved the literature into seventeen conceptual clusters.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A keyword analysis identified seven conceptual clusters
statements.note: Seven clusters were identified, not seventeen.

statements.text: Publications from the United States were most often funded by the National Institutes of Health.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The analysis encompassed an evaluation of publication volume, contributing authors, influential journals, country and institutional contributions, and citation metrics.
statements.note: The metrics evaluated did not include funding sources.

statements.text: The United States led on both publication volume and citation frequency, with China next and Italy third.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The United States is the leading country in terms of both publication volume and citation frequency, followed by China and Italy.
statements.note: The country ranking is as stated.

statements.text: A 26-bp promoter indel tunes CDCA7 expression in natural populations and sets the degree of CG methylation and transposable element silencing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identify a 26-bp promoter indel modulating CDCA7 expression in natural populations and determining the degree of mCG and transposable element silencing.
statements.note: The indel size and its two consequences are reported.

statements.text: Plants carrying the low-expression CDCA7 allele flowered later than those with the high-expression allele.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The geographic distribution of CDCA7 alleles suggests that new alleles have repeatedly expanded to novel ecological niches, indicating a potential role in local adaptation.
statements.note: Allele distribution hints at adaptation; no phenotype such as flowering time is measured.

statements.text: CDCA7 or its paralogue binds the chromatin remodeller DDM1, which gives methyltransferases access to DNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: CDCA7 or its paralogue physically binds the chromatin remodeller DECREASE IN DNA METHYLATION 1 (DDM1), which facilitates access of methyltransferases to DNA.
statements.note: The interaction and DDM1's role are stated.

statements.text: The predominant function of CDCA7 proteins is maintaining CHH methylation rather than CG methylation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: while CDCA7 proteins control all DDM1-dependent processes, their predominant function is the maintenance of mCG
statements.note: Their predominant function is maintenance of CG methylation.

statements.text: Ty3 retrotransposon expression rose markedly in the axolotl with chronological age.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: it is shown that Ty3 retrotransposons are highly upregulated in the axolotl as an effect of chronological aging
statements.note: Stated as the aging result.

statements.text: The blastema failed to readjust most of the transposon differential expression seen in adulthood.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Although the blastema can readjust most of the transposon differential expression in adulthood, several elements remain affected
statements.note: The blastema does readjust most of it, with only several elements still affected.

statements.text: Suppressing Ty3 expression in older axolotls restored their regenerative fidelity.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum) has a great capacity to regenerate its tissues; however, the fidelity and success of its regenerative process diminish with age.
statements.note: The age-related decline is described, but no intervention on transposon expression is tested.

statements.text: During limb regeneration, Ty3 expression and the associated pathways were clearly downregulated.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: By contrast, it is found that during regeneration of the limb, these pathways and the expression of Ty3 retrotransposons are distinctly downregulated.
statements.note: This is the reported regeneration result.

statements.text: Pathways for cellular stress, nucleic acid sensing and innate immune signalling were upregulated in UV-exposed cell lines and in pterygium alike.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We found that pathways involved in cellular stress, nucleic acid sensing, and innate immune signaling were upregulated in both cell lines exposed to increased amounts of UV energy as well as pterygium.
statements.note: Both settings showed the same upregulation.

statements.text: Blocking cGAS signalling in conjunctival fibroblasts prevented the UV-induced inflammatory response.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We propose that UV triggers the de-repression of transposable elements (TEs), including endogenous retroviruses (ERVs), and subsequently activate double-stranded RNA and DNA sensors such as RIG-I and cGAS.
statements.note: Sensor activation is proposed from expression data; no inhibition experiment is reported.

statements.text: Cultured human conjunctival fibroblasts were exposed to a single UV intensity on one day only.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: cultured human conjunctival fibroblasts exposed over multiple days to a range of UV intensities
statements.note: Exposure ran over multiple days across a range of intensities.

statements.text: The study also found transposable elements to be differentially expressed.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We also observed differential expression of TEs.
statements.note: Differential TE expression is reported as a result.
